sections.h2: Where Kalamazoo County land records are filed
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits in the County Administration Building at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49007. The phone is 269-383-8970. It is a constitutional office dating from 1835, and recording a document makes it public without making it legally valid.

Staff index and preserve the records, nothing more: title searches and legal advice are off limits. In most sales the title company either walks the deed in or e-records it. If you file on your own, read the formatting checklist below, because the counter turns away papers that miss a rule.

All four cities (Galesburg, Kalamazoo, Parchment and Portage) and all five villages (Augusta, Climax, Richland, Schoolcraft and Vicksburg) record at this single office.

Recording costs $30 a document under MCL 600.2567. Extras that can apply:

  • $3 more for each added instrument on a paper that assigns or discharges several.
  • Copies at $1 a page, plus $5 a document if certified.
  • $5 per search when staff look something up.
  • A $5 treasurer certificate covering up to 20 tax ID numbers on one document, then 20 cents for each description after that.

Payment options at the counter are cash, check, money order or card. Recording checks are payable to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds and certificate checks to the treasurer involved. There is no online payment portal for counter filings, so card payers phone the office or come in. The full list is on the county fee schedule.

The seller owes transfer tax, and it is paid at the counter when the deed goes on record. The state act names the seller as the taxpayer in MCL 207.523, and the county rate comes from MCL 207.504. Both are applied to a price rounded up to the next $500.

Kalamazoo County transfer tax rates
TaxRate per $1,000Same rate per $500
County$1.1055 cents
State$7.50$3.75

A chart on the county website covers other prices, and the site links exemption lists for both taxes.

sections.h2: Deeds that need a tax certificate
sections.html:
When the grantor "warrants" or "defends" the title in the deed, the treasurer must clear the taxes first. On the county's list are warranty and covenant deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments with warranty wording, and master deeds, amendments adding property to a condominium among them. The rule comes from MCL 211.135.

Inside the City of Kalamazoo there is one more step. You obtain a city certificate from the City Treasurer at Kalamazoo City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036, for $10. The County Treasurer issues its own only after that.

Unpaid taxes block clearance until the balance is settled at closing. Get the payoff amount early, since delinquent balances gather interest every month.

sections.h2: What a document must look like
sections.html:
Layout is governed by MCL 565.201, and the county FAQ turns it into a checklist:

  • White copy paper, letter or legal size.
  • Black ink, 10 point type or larger.
  • A clear 2.5 inch strip across the top of page one, the document type printed on the first line below it, and half inch margins elsewhere.
  • A notary for the deed types the county lists, including warranty, quitclaim, executor, trustee and sheriff's deeds. Witnesses are no longer required.
  • Court documents bearing the court's certification and seal.

Rejected papers are returned with a letter giving the reason, and you fix and refile. Changing the names on a deed means a new deed. The office cannot prepare it for you, so call an attorney or title agency.

E-recording runs through four certified vendors: Simplifile, Indecomm, ePN and CSC. Submissions are worked on county business days. Money moves by ACH under the vendor's agreement, and a vendor can tack on its own processing fee. Plats and master deeds with full size maps cannot be sent this way.

Michigan's statewide e-recording standards took effect on January 1, 2014, and the county follows them. The title company submits the deed, so sellers seldom meet a vendor.

A Consumer E-Recording portal serves one time filers with affidavits, discharges, mortgages, certificates of trust, liens and releases. Ownership transfers such as deeds, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are not accepted there. For a deed, go to the counter or a title company.

Start with the Document Searches page on kalcounty.gov. The Deeds Search tool is free for index searching, then costs $1 a page plus a processing fee to view, print or save an image. Tapestry EON, available since October 21, 2024, costs $8.75 per search. Laredo is a monthly subscription aimed at frequent users such as title professionals.

Staff can pull your latest deed for $5 a property and $1 a page, with certification for another $5. Public workstations in the Administration Building let you search grantor and grantee names free, with printing at $1 a page. Search by name, since recorded papers need no address.

Land record images reach back to 1831, though the complete index only starts in 1984. For a long chain of title, a title company search is the safer route.

Surviving owners do not need a new deed. Recording an official death certificate with this office shows that the deceased owner's interest has ended, and the certificate becomes part of the title chain. Photocopies of death certificates are refused.

County staff cannot tell heirs what authority they need to sell, so put that question to the title company. A free fraud alert is also available: register a personal or business name and you hear whenever a matching document is recorded. That is handy for an empty inherited house.

Selling an inherited house

Collect the death certificate, recorded deed, and any payoff or tax statements first. A cash sale skips the repairs and showings of a traditional listing, which suits an estate that wants to finish quickly.

A title company or closing attorney drafts the deed, subtracts transfer tax from what you net and delivers everything to the Register of Deeds. For a City of Kalamazoo address, both treasurer certificates are requested ahead of filing, so build that extra step into your closing timeline.

Filing on your own means carrying an original notarized deed, a $30 check, the transfer tax and one more check per treasurer certificate. Not sure what type of deed you hold? Phone 269-383-8970 first, because the type decides whether a certificate is needed.

sections.h2: Kalamazoo County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Kalamazoo County has 263,795 residents and 116,117 housing units. Owners live in 64.5 percent of occupied homes, so many sellers here are landlords. The middle home value is $241,800, median gross rent is $1,093 a month, and median household income is $72,532 in 2024 dollars.

Owners outside the city limits record here as well. Ask the township or village treasurer about local tax.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Kalamazoo County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document. Transfer tax and treasurer certificates are billed separately, and a paper discharging several instruments adds $3 per extra one.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax my bill as a seller?
faqs.a: Yes, paid at the Register of Deeds counter when the deed is recorded. The county charges $1.10 and the state $7.50 for every $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Does a house in the city of Kalamazoo need two tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. A parcel within city limits pays $10 for the city certificate first, then $5 for the county one.

faqs.q: Are witnesses required on a Kalamazoo County deed?
faqs.a: No. A notary is the requirement now, for warranty, quitclaim and most other deed types.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by card?
faqs.a: Yes, by calling 269-383-8970 or paying at the counter at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue. There is no online payment portal for counter recordings.
